text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.

- Croatia promises to publish list of 1991 Serb war crimes suspects from Eastern Slavonia who will be banned from voting in local elections in April, President Tudjman says in meeting with U.N. administrattor Jacques Klein.
- Ministry of Health will have final say in approving maximum prices of imported and domestic drugs under a draft law, says deputy Health Minister Zeljko Riner.
- Number of jobless in Croatia in January, estimated at 18,000, is 6.9 percent higher than a year ago, according to Labour Institute.

- Some Croatian banks are inflating interest rates on their loans. By charging interest rates on the entire sum in advance, they are pushing interest rates up to 18 from 10 percent, says Reiffeisen Bank in Zagreb.
- Over 80 kilometres of new roads were built in the past year, says Transport Minister Zeljko Luzavec. Before 1990, the annual rate was 10 km.
- Bavaria signs a letter of intent to invest between 350 and 400 million German marks in Croatian part of Phyrn-Nuremberg-Linz-Graz-Maribor-Zagreb highway.

- Lord Northampton sold collection of 14 antiquities originating from Istria worth at least 80 million pounds. The collection, known as Seus treasury, was dug out in 1980 and smuggled to Geneva by the former Yugoslav army.
